n: Prepaid Cards and Stored Value Abuse
ds: Prepaid cards and digital stored-value products can be loaded, transferred and cashed out quickly, sometimes with limited customer identification. Criminals use them to move small amounts at scale, convert cash, receive fraud proceeds and fund illicit purchases, often via many cards or mule holders.

src.t: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Prepaid Cards, Mobile Payments and Internet-Based Payment Services (2013)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)

rat: Bulk loads and cash-out of prepaid cards by many holders or mules.

ind.n: Bulk purchase of cards by one person or entity
ind.cx: One buyer acquires many cards, often in cash, with a common funding source or shipping address.
ind.ds: Large volumes of prepaid cards or gift cards are purchased or sold.
ind.cn: Bulk purchase or sale of cards or vouchers

ind.n: Cards funded by many unrelated third parties
ind.cx: Multiple unconnected payers load one card or small set of cards.
ind.ds: Numerous unrelated payers send frequent, often small, payments to one account, wallet or beneficiary, or one funder pays many beneficiaries, with no clear commercial relationship.
ind.cn: Many unrelated senders paying a single account or recipient

ind.n: Loads immediately followed by foreign ATM withdrawals
ind.cx: Funds are drawn down in cash overseas or in high-risk locations soon after loading.
ind.ds: Funds are drawn down in cash overseas or in high-risk locations soon after loading.

ind.n: Repeated loads just below identification thresholds
ind.cx: Multiple loads sized to avoid enhanced verification.
ind.ds: Repeated transfers, remittances or card/wallet loads kept just below an identification, record-keeping or travel-rule threshold.
ind.cn: Non-cash transfers or loads just below identification or reporting thresholds

ind.cx: Different cardholders share phone, address, email or device.
ind.ds: Unrelated customers or applicants share the same phone, email, address, device or bank account, including mail drops and shared accommodation.
ind.cn: Multiple customers sharing contact details or addresses

ind.n: Anonymous or minimally verified cards with high turnover
ind.cx: Cards without full ID show large inflows and outflows inconsistent with low-limit design.
ind.ds: Prepaid cards or stored-value products without full ID, with high load limits, cross-border use or turnover inconsistent with design.
ind.cn: Anonymous or lightly verified prepaid or stored-value instruments

ind.n: Card used to pay high-risk online merchants
ind.cx: Spend concentrates at gambling, darknet-adjacent or unlicensed merchants.
ind.ds: Spend concentrates at gambling, darknet-adjacent or unlicensed merchants.

ind.n: Rapid transfers of stored value between wallets then cash-out
ind.cx: Funds hop across stored-value accounts to peer wallets, then to cash or crypto.
ind.ds: Stored value or funds move quickly between wallets or cards and are then cashed out.
ind.cn: Rapid stored-value or wallet hops then cash-out

ind.n: Cards received by mules and redirected abroad
ind.cx: Cards shipped to freight forwarders or mail drops, then used elsewhere.
ind.ds: Goods or cards are shipped to freight forwarders, reshippers, mail drops or addresses with no storage or sales operations or link to the buyer.
ind.cn: Delivery to forwarder, mailbox or address unrelated to buyer

ind.cx: Loads via cards or accounts reported stolen, followed by cash-out.
ind.ds: Loads via cards or accounts reported stolen, followed by cash-out.

ctl.n: Duplicate and synthetic identity checks at onboarding
ctl.ds: Compares new applicant identifiers such as name, email, phone, address, device and bank account with existing customers, previously declined or exited applicants and known-bad data. Matches are blocked or referred, limiting repeat applicants, synthetic identities and mule recruitment.

Caps transaction size, frequency, load, withdrawal and deposit values, with staged increases as legitimate behaviour is established and per-customer limits at kiosks. It bounds the loss and laundering capacity of new or higher-risk accounts.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

ctl.n: Specialist investigation and suspicious activity reporting
ctl.ds: Trained analysts investigate alerts with typology playbooks, document rationale and file reports where suspicion is formed, with prompt reporting to the competent authority. It converts alerts into actionable intelligence.

Detects use of VPN, proxy and anonymising services and compares access geolocation with declared residence and sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions. It reveals concealed location and supports geographic restrictions.
Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

Checks identity and supporting documents for tampering, forgery, template reuse and internal inconsistency, and corroborates their data against authoritative or reliable independent sources. It exposes altered or counterfeit credentials that pass a visual check.

ctl.n: Risk appetite and product policy statements
ctl.ds: Documents the institution's appetite and permitted or prohibited products, assets and activities for a given risk area, with limits and review cadence. It gives staff and systems a clear boundary for acceptance.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.

Monitors merchant-level patterns such as ticket size, refund, void and chargeback rates, descriptor mismatch and cross-merchant flows. It identifies transaction laundering, bust-out and illicit merchants.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
